answer: The tundra cap is enforced at intake and signal publishes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a fleet in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because every identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a ripple tag. That is 3 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
